Polish Utilities Sector Sees Innovation with Launch of SmartFlow Meter

Warsaw – The Polish gas and water utilities sector welcomed a new era of innovation today as EnergoWod, a leading regional manufacturer, launched its much-anticipated SmartFlow Meter at a press event in the capital. The product aims to modernise metering infrastructure for utility providers and consumers across Poland.

The SmartFlow Meter is designed to provide real-time consumption data, leak detection, and automated billing integration for both gas and water supply networks. According to EnergoWod representatives, the device is compatible with existing infrastructure and is expected to help utilities reduce losses and improve service reliability.

“We are proud to introduce a product developed in Poland that addresses the challenges faced by utility companies and end-users alike,” said Marek Nowicki, EnergoWod’s Director of Product Development, during the launch event. “Our SmartFlow Meter offers a new level of transparency and efficiency, supporting the national push towards smart city solutions and environmental responsibility.”

Poland’s utilities sector has been undergoing steady modernisation, with several cities embracing digital technologies for better management of resources. Industry analysts estimate that non-revenue water—water lost before it reaches consumers—exceeds 15% in some Polish municipalities. Gas utilities face similar challenges with loss detection and accurate billing.

“The introduction of advanced metering solutions is a positive step,” noted Agnieszka Sienkiewicz, an analyst at the Central European Utilities Forum. “Automated data collection not only benefits providers through more accurate readings but also empowers consumers to better understand and control their usage.”

EnergoWod reports the SmartFlow Meter is already undergoing pilot installations in Białystok and Gdańsk. Feedback from these projects will inform the broader rollout scheduled for later this year. Local officials in Białystok expressed support for the initiative, citing potential reductions in operational costs and improvements in consumer service.

Janusz Pawlak, chair of the Polish Gas & Water Workers’ Union, welcomed the new technology, saying, “Our members are eager to work with innovative tools that make their jobs safer and more efficient, while delivering better outcomes for households and businesses.”

As Poland continues to invest in critical infrastructure upgrades, the launch of the SmartFlow Meter highlights the sector’s commitment to innovation and operational excellence.
